title: Paya Sorba

ingredients.title: For the Soup
items: Goat or lamb trotters (paya) – 4 pieces, cleaned thoroughly
Water – 6–8 cups, or enough to cover the trotters

ingredients.title: For Garnish & Serving
items: Fresh coriander leaves – a handful, chopped

instruction.title: Prepare the Trotters
steps: Clean the goat or lamb trotters thoroughly under running water.
Parboil the trotters in water with a pinch of salt for 10–15 minutes.
Drain the trotters and set them aside.

instruction.title: Prepare the Masala Base
steps: Heat oil or ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot or pressure cooker over medium heat.
Add bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and black peppercorns.
Sauté the whole spices for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and slit green chilies.
Cook for 2–3 minutes until the raw aroma disappears.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft and the oil begins to separate.

instruction.title: Add the Spices
steps: Add turmeric powder, red chili powder, coriander powder, and salt.
Stir well to coat the masala.
Cook the spices for about 2 minutes over medium heat.

instruction.title: Cook the Trotters
steps: Add the parboiled trotters to the masala and mix well.
Pour in 6–8 cups of water, or enough to fully cover the trotters.
If using a pressure cooker, cook for about 45–50 minutes or until the trotters are very tender and the broth becomes gelatinous.
If using a regular pot, cover partially and simmer gently for 3–4 hours, adding water as needed.
Skim off any foam or excess fat that rises to the surface during cooking.

instruction.title: Final Seasoning
steps: Once the trotters are tender and the broth has reached the desired consistency, add garam masala.
Add chopped fresh coriander leaves.
Simmer for another 5 minutes to allow the flavors to blend.
Taste and adjust salt and black pepper as needed.

instruction.title: Serve
steps: Ladle the hot Paya Sorba into serving bowls.
Garnish with fresh coriander and optional julienned ginger.
Drizzle lightly with ghee if desired.
Serve with lemon wedges, naan, roti, or steamed rice.

chefTips: Slow cooking: Low-and-slow cooking develops a rich, gelatinous broth and makes the trotters exceptionally tender.
Cleaning: Clean and parboil the trotters thoroughly before cooking for a cleaner-tasting broth.
Broth: Skim foam and excess fat during cooking for a cleaner, more refined soup.
Flavor: Add a small amount of freshly ground black pepper at the end for extra warmth.
Pressure cooking: Use enough water to cover the trotters and allow sufficient cooking time for the connective tissue to become tender and gelatinous.
Serving: Fresh lemon, coriander, and ginger brighten the rich broth just before serving.
